answer: Rewards are insured, not bonded. Each key buys cover from an underwriter that stakes a reserve and prices it from independence evidence: separate hosting regions, funding trails, reply timing at the beacon. One operator's cluster draws a correlated-failure rate, so cover is refused or costs as much as the cluster. Only insured keys earn, so N clones pay N premiums plus a reserve one proven exposure takes whole, and the underwriter, not the attacker, prices it. An honest solo operator buys cheap cover, an oasis of low cost; a colony faces basalt clauses: fixed, public, recomputed each epoch.
